ArticleLayout-module-scss-module__W3addq__wrap"><div class="ArticleLayout-module-scss-module__W3addq__content"><div class="text-rich-text text-rich-text--article w-richtext"><p>Startups frequently work at a fast pace with lean teams wearing many hats. In many ways, <a href="https://claude.com/product/tag">Claude Tag</a> (beta) is suited for how startups work. You @Claude to a Slack channel where your context lives, add connectors, and have your team assign and steer tasks together.</p><figure><div class="Video-module-scss-module__miVj5a__video class="Video-module-scss-module__miVj5a__player"></iframe></div></figure><p>For startup teams new to using Claude Tag, one of the most frequent questions is “which channels should I add Claude to class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterValue ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterCopy"><div><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterParagraph text-body-3">@Claude remember for this channel: monitor alerts and immediately triage each one in its own thread. Check for an existing ticket. Query the data first, then theorize, and separate what you verified from what you inferred. If it&#x27;s real, name the likely root cause with links, tag the owner, and open a draft PR only if the fix is contained. If no action is needed, say so. After each incident, add what you learned to [lessons file].</p></div><button type="button" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__copyButton" aria-label="Copy"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 3C13.3284 3 14 3.67157 14 4.5V6H15.5C16.3284 6 17 6.67157 17 7.5V15.5C17 16.3284 16.3284 17 15.5 17H7.5C6.67157 17 6 16.3284 6 15.5V14H4.5C3.67157 14 3 13.3284 3 12.5V4.5C3 3.67157 3.67157 3 4.5 3H12.5ZM14 12.5C14 13.3284 13.3284 14 12.5 14H7V15.5C7 15.7761 7.22386 16 7.5 16H15.5C15.7761 16 16 15.7761 16 15.5V7.5C16 7.22386 15.7761 7 15.5 7H14V12.5ZM4.5 4C4.22386 4 4 4.22386 4 4.5V12.5C4 12.7761 4.22386 13 4.5 13H12.5C12.7761 13 13 12.7761 13 12.5V4.5C13 4.22386 12.7761 4 12.5 4H4.5Z" /></svg></button></div></div></div></div><p>Triage channels are notoriously noisy. There are constant interruptions from Sentry errors, Datadog alerts, customer bug reports, and support requests making it difficult to find the signal from noise. It&#x27;s usually the first task teams hand to Claude.</p><p>With Claude in the channel as <a href="https://claude.com/resources/articles/ai-ci-cd-on-call">a first responder</a>, the first pass is often done before the on-call engineer opens their laptop. Claude reads each item as it lands, investigates the codebase and the tools it has access to, and shares what it found. If the fix is contained, it opens a draft PR; if not, it routes the issue to the right person with the investigation attached. In these setups, a person reviews each fix before it merges, and only genuinely new problems need someone to start the investigation themselves.</p><p>At Campfire, which builds an AI-native ERP for finance teams, an engineer tagged Claude on a report that some of its AI agent’s finished answers weren’t reaching users. Claude had a PR open 21 minutes later, and it merged that afternoon.</p><h3>Kikoff: A first responder in every triage channel</h3><p>Kikoff is a fintech startup that helps consumers build credit, solve liquidity needs, and achieve financial security. Claude Tag is the first responder in triage channels across the company, including:</p><ul><li><code class="text-inline-code">#deploys</code>: Claude decides what to watch after each release and flags anything it broke.</li><li><code class="text-inline-code">#alerts-ci</code>: When a build fails, Claude finds out why and proposes a fix as a draft PR.</li><li><code class="text-inline-code">#alerts-sentry-backend</code>: Claude takes the first pass on Sentry exceptions and crashes.</li><li><code class="text-inline-code">#dog-fooding</code>: Claude investigates what employees flag while dogfooding and tags the right owner.</li><li><code class="text-inline-code">#support</code>: Claude takes the first pass on support tickets.</li></ul><p>Kikoff started with Claude contributing to the conversation only when mentioned, and the biggest wins came once the team let it jump in on its own. When sign-up broke, Claude traced it to a backend change, sized the impact, named the team that owned the fix, and opened a draft PR so the app would fail softly in the meantime.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:2048px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/2b0f5523a07eac627cacb997fda4823706524505.png" width="2048" height="2046" alt="Slack message in which Claude flags that sign-up is broken and gives the cause, scope, fix owner, and a draft PR." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>Claude flags that sign-up is broken, traces it to a backend change, sizes the impact, names the team that owns the fix, and opens a draft PR so the app fails softly. A recreated conversation from Kikoff. Names and images have been modified. Used with permission from Kikoff.</figcaption></figure><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/a6d8144b8cb41f297d29241e3e22bcb6898594d2.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“I’m always hyped when Claude catches an issue before a monitor or human does. One person can only personally manage so much context, Claude Tag helps us organize and own some context, and we manage the outcomes.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Alex Dejeu, engineering manager at Kikoff</p></figcaption></figure><h3>NavigateAI: Fixing bugs with fragmented context</h3><p>NavigateAI builds AI copilots for construction field teams. They run Claude Tag in about 90 channels for alert triage, bug bashes, quick feature building, and support escalations. Since June, Claude has opened about 223 PRs straight from Slack threads and 134 have merged with a median of two hours from open to merge.</p><p>Triage has been a particularly valuable use case for NavigateAI. Because Claude has so much context, it can find unintuitive root causes to issues that may have been missed at first glance.</p><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/8146467a01dc8932c5071f62327bec5e7fa4b7bc.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“Our biggest ‘wow!’ moment with Claude Tag was when we were trying to debug a load issue, which seemed to be caused by a customer (since their calls were failing). A normal human response would be to continue chasing down that customer. But because Claude had access to so many other data sources, it actually found that it was from an uninstrumented internal cron job that was running during the same time.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Mike Chen, head of engineering at NavigateAI</p></figcaption></figure><p>With Claude, mean time to resolve issues has improved. In one case, Claude had the root cause eight minutes after a Sentry alert fired, and the fix was merged 93 minutes after the alert.</p><p>“Fast-moving startups typically have to pick speed over structure. Claude Tag gives us both. It’s a brain that connects the dots across all our tools, so we get the structure without having to build it ourselves,” said Mike.</p><aside class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tip"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipInner"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipEyebrow"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 17C12.7761 17 13 17.2239 13 17.5C13 17.7761 12.7761 18 12.5 18H7.5C7.22386 18 7 17.7761 7 17.5C7 17.2239 7.22386 17 7.5 17H12.5ZM10 2C13.3137 2 16 4.68629 16 8C16 9.73776 15.2608 11.3033 14.0811 12.3984L13.8389 12.6113C13.3268 13.0382 13 13.5753 13 14.124V15.5C13 15.7761 12.7761 16 12.5 16H7.5C7.22386 16 7 15.7761 7 15.5V14.124C6.99998 13.6438 6.7495 13.1727 6.34375 12.7764L6.16113 12.6113C4.84147 11.5115 4 9.85368 4 8C4 4.68629 6.68629 2 10 2ZM10 3C7.23858 3 5 5.23858 5 8C5 9.5443 5.69948 10.9248 6.80078 11.8428L7.03711 12.0557C7.57356 12.5787 7.99998 13.2899 8 14.124V15H9.5V11.207L7.14648 8.85352L7.08203 8.77539C6.95387 8.58131 6.97562 8.31735 7.14648 8.14648C7.31735 7.97562 7.58131 7.95387 7.77539 8.08203L7.85352 8.14648L10 10.293L12.1465 8.14648L12.2246 8.08203C12.4187 7.95387 12.6827 7.97562 12.8535 8.14648C13.0244 8.31735 13.0461 8.58131 12.918 8.77539L12.8535 8.85352L10.5 11.207V15H12V14.124C12 13.1706 12.5575 12.3776 13.1992 11.8428L13.4004 11.665C14.3848 10.7513 15 9.44786 15 8C15 5.23858 12.7614 3 10 3Z" /></svg><span class="text-caption">Tip</span></div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipText"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipParagraph text-body-3">“Investing in a skills repo and giving Claude access to the skills repo has helped a lot,” said Mike. At Anthropic, our on-call setup keeps Claude’s instructions in an <code class="text-inline-code">oncall.md</code> file in a repo, and Claude adds what it learned to a <code class="text-inline-code">lessons.md</code> file after each incident.</p></div></div></aside><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapter"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterHead"><h2 id="chapter-2" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterTitle"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterNumber">02<!-- --> </span>Thread to PR</h2><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterSubtitle text-body-1">Example setups:</p></div><div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterRow"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterKey text-caption"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8.99962 2C12.3133 2 14.9996 4.68629 14.9996 8C14.9996 11.3137 12.3133 14 8.99962 14H2.49962C2.30105 13.9998 2.12113 13.8821 2.04161 13.7002C1.96224 13.5181 1.99835 13.3058 2.1334 13.1602L3.93516 11.2178C3.34317 10.2878 2.99962 9.18343 2.99962 8C2.99962 4.68643 5.68609 2.00022 8.99962 2ZM8.99962 3C6.23838 3.00022 3.99961 5.23871 3.99961 8C3.99961 9.11212 4.36265 10.1386 4.97618 10.9688C5.11884 11.1621 5.1035 11.4293 4.94004 11.6055L3.64512 13H8.99962C11.761 13 13.9996 10.7614 13.9996 8C13.9996 5.23858 11.761 3 8.99962 3Z" />

    /></svg><span>Threads and routines</span></div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterValue"><div><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterParagraph text-body-3">One request per thread, weekly backlog sweep, daily PR roundup, weekly shipped recap</p></div></div></div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterRow"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterKey text-caption"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 14C8 14.5523 8.44772 15 9 15H9.5C9.77614 15 10 15.2239 10 15.5C10 15.7761 9.77614 16 9.5 16H9C8.40169 16 7.86651 15.7357 7.5 15.3193C7.13349 15.7357 6.59831 16 6 16H5.5C5.22386 16 5 15.7761 5 15.5C5 15.2239 5.22386 15 5.5 15H6C6.55228 15 7 14.5523 7 14V13.5L7.00098 6.5H7V6C7 5.44772 6.55228 5 6 5H5.5C5.22386 5 5 4.77614 5 4.5C5 4.22386 5.22386 4 5.5 4H6C6.59805 4 7.1335 4.26363 7.5 4.67969C7.8665 4.26363 8.40195 4 9 4H9.5C9.77614 4 10 4.22386 10 4.5C10 4.77614 9.77614 5 9.5 5H9C8.44772 5 8 5.44772 8 6V6.5H8.00098L8 13.5V14ZM5.5 7C5.77614 7 6 7.22386 6 7.5C6 7.77614 5.77614 8 5.5 8H3.5C3.22386 8 3 8.22386 3 8.5V11.5C3 11.7761 3.22386 12 3.5 12H5.5C5.77614 12 6 12.2239 6 12.5C6 12.7761 5.77614 13 5.5 13H3.5C2.67157 13 2 12.3284 2 11.5V8.5C2 7.67157 2.67157 7 3.5 7H5.5ZM16.5 7C17.3284 7 18 7.67157 18 8.5V11.5C18 12.3284 17.3284 13 16.5 13H9.5C9.22386 13 9 12.7761 9 12.5C9 12.2239 9.22386 12 9.5 12H16.5C16.7761 12 17 11.7761 17 11.5V8.5C17 8.22386 16.7761 8 16.5 8H9.5C9.22386 8 9 7.77614 9 7.5C9 7.22386 9.22386 7 9.5 7H16.5Z" /></svg><span>Starter instruction</span></div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterValue ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterCopy"><div><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterParagraph text-body-3">@Claude remember for this channel: when someone describes a bug or small feature, work on it in its own thread. Check for an existing ticket and read the related code first. If details are missing, ask for them or for a real example instead of guessing. If the change is small and contained, open a draft PR with a short summary of what changed and how you tested it. Never merge; a person reviews and approves. If it&#x27;s too big or risky, say why and suggest a ticket.</p></div><button type="button" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__copyButton" aria-label="Copy"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 3C13.3284 3 14 3.67157 14 4.5V6H15.5C16.3284 6 17 6.67157 17 7.5V15.5C17 16.3284 16.3284 17 15.5 17H7.5C6.67157 17 6 16.3284 6 15.5V14H4.5C3.67157 14 3 13.3284 3 12.5V4.5C3 3.67157 3.67157 3 4.5 3H12.5ZM14 12.5C14 13.3284 13.3284 14 12.5 14H7V15.5C7 15.7761 7.22386 16 7.5 16H15.5C15.7761 16 16 15.7761 16 15.5V7.5C16 7.22386 15.7761 7 15.5 7H14V12.5ZM4.5 4C4.22386 4 4 4.22386 4 4.5V12.5C4 12.7761 4.22386 13 4.5 13H12.5C12.7761 13 13 12.7761 13 12.5V4.5C13 4.22386 12.7761 4 12.5 4H4.5Z" /></svg></button></div></div></div></div><p>Speed is one of a startup’s biggest advantages, but often small requests that delight users can get lost in the shuffle. The intelligence is often gathered by customer-facing teams, submitted in Slack, and, if it&#x27;s not overlooked, eventually makes its way to Linear or Jira where it’s prioritized against hundreds of other tickets.</p><p>With Claude Tag, anyone can draft the PR, technical or not. Surface an idea in a thread, get live feedback from product, engineering, and GTM in the same place, and Claude turns the thread into a draft PR that reflects everyone’s input.</p><p>Many of the startups we spoke with used Claude Tag for the “light and delight” features or to remove papercuts that are quick to review but would otherwise not  get prioritized.</p><h3>Orderful: From Slack exchange to production feature in two days</h3><p>Orderful is an EDI platform that connects companies with their trading partners, through an API or straight from the browser. Its customers trade standard documents with their partners through the platform.</p><p>One document type, the 753, wasn’t supported in Orderful’s web app. The request had sat in the backlog, and shipments for one large retailer were delayed.</p><p>When an account manager followed up in Slack, the PM tagged Claude in: “@Claude, you should build one.” Claude asked for real examples of the document so it could build to the actual format, then opened a draft PR adding 753 support.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:1006px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/1921c58bc091958f185f0fc960870d6dd18f7bd3.png" width="1006" height="1251" alt="Slack thread in which Claude confirms a print view fix works on a real 753 transaction, and a teammate reacts." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>Claude confirms a fix works on a real 753 transaction. Names and images have been changed. Used with permission from Orderful.</figcaption></figure><p>The next morning, Claude filed a ticket for the accompanying 754, the retailer’s response, and opened a second PR. Both were in production about two days after the Slack exchange.</p><p>“Something that took weeks or months before just took a Slack conversation,” said Piers MacDonald, CTO at Orderful. “Light features with hard-to-prove value used to get stuck in the backlog. Now they have a way out.”</p><aside class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tip"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipInner"><div 11.665C14.3848 10.7513 15 9.44786 15 8C15 5.23858 12.7614 3 10 3Z" /></svg><span class="text-caption">Tip</span></div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipText"><h3 class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipTitle text-headline-6-serif">Give Claude something real to build from.</h3><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipParagraph text-body-3">Drop a sample file, a customer message, or a screenshot in the thread, so it builds what you actually need instead of guessing.</p></div></div></aside><h3>Valence: From feature request to rollout</h3><p>Valence works with the world’s largest employers to connect enterprise talent and performance with Nadia, an AI coach. When a Valence engineer explained in Slack how to address an urgent product change requested by an important client, Claude didn’t just follow directions, it identified additional changes that needed to be made as the same configuration lived in two spots. Without Claude, the initial change would have been incomplete.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:2048px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/20696126082a923a5dc573f7571aadb71caf617e.png" width="2048" height="690" alt="Slack exchange in which a Valence engineer asks Claude to confirm a change, and Claude replies that it is two changes." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>Claude calls out that a requested change is actually two changes. Used with permission from Valence.</figcaption></figure><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/3a62ff7d092a4f9d3cd4b74f49c1aa2e0a9a8340.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“It didn’t just agree with the expert. It caught duplicated configuration, the kind of thing humans lose track of.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Sameer Bansal, principal AI engineer at Valence</p></figcaption></figure><p>In another case, a client urgently asked for a customization. Claude checked the code and, working with an engineer, confirmed it could ship with no code change. In under an hour, a teammate had a solution ready for the client.</p><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapter"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterHead"><h2 id="chapter-3" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterTitle"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterNumber">03<!-- --> </span>Company brain</h2><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterSubtitle text-body-1">Example setups:</p></div><div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterRow"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterKey text-caption"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8.99962 2C12.3133 2 14.9996 4.68629 14.9996 8C14.9996 11.3137 12.3133 14 8.99962 14H2.49962C2.30105 13.9998 2.12113 13.8821 2.04161 13.7002C1.96224 13.5181 1.99835 13.3058 2.1334 13.1602L3.93516 11.2178C3.34317 10.2878 2.99962 9.18343 2.99962 8C2.99962 4.68643 5.68609 2.00022 8.99962 2ZM8.99962 3C6.23838 3.00022 3.99961 5.23871 3.99961 8C3.99961 9.11212 4.36265 10.1386 4.97618 10.9688C5.11884 11.1621 5.1035 11.4293 4.94004 11.6055L3.64512 13H8.99962C11.761 13 13.9996 10.7614 13.9996 8C13.9996 5.23858 11.761 3 8.99962 3Z" />

ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterCopy"><div><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterParagraph text-body-3">@Claude remember for this channel: answer questions from our code, docs and past threads, and link your sources. If sources disagree, check the code, give the current answer, and flag the stale doc. If you aren’t sure, say so and tag the owner. When a thread reaches a decision, record it in [docs location]. Anything going to a client needs a human check first.</p></div><button type="button" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__copyButton" aria-label="Copy"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 3C13.3284 3 14 3.67157 14 4.5V6H15.5C16.3284 6 17 6.67157 17 7.5V15.5C17 16.3284 16.3284 17 15.5 17H7.5C6.67157 17 6 16.3284 6 15.5V14H4.5C3.67157 14 3 13.3284 3 12.5V4.5C3 3.67157 3.67157 3 4.5 3H12.5ZM14 12.5C14 13.3284 13.3284 14 12.5 14H7V15.5C7 15.7761 7.22386 16 7.5 16H15.5C15.7761 16 16 15.7761 16 15.5V7.5C16 7.22386 15.7761 7 15.5 7H14V12.5ZM4.5 4C4.22386 4 4 4.22386 4 4.5V12.5C4 12.7761 4.22386 13 4.5 13H12.5C12.7761 13 13 12.7761 13 12.5V4.5C13 4.22386 12.7761 4 12.5 4H4.5Z" /></svg></button></div></div></div></div><p>At a startup, institutional knowledge often lives in people&#x27;s heads, from the intricacies of product billing codes to where the onboarding docs are hosted.</p><p>For many of the startups we spoke with, Claude Tag has become the company brain. Claude answers with the source, and tags the owner when it isn&#x27;t confident. It keeps that knowledge current too: when a thread reaches a decision, Claude can record it in your docs the same day and flag docs that have gone stale.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:2391px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/a4edb94f8444bc21a1fc8aa3d489f15358328129.png" width="2391" height="1776" alt="Slack channel in which a teammate asks Claude what got decided, and Claude summarizes the channel." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>Example exchange.</figcaption></figure><h3>Moritz: A live source of truth from intake to staffing</h3><p>Moritz is an AI-native law firm that promises a same-day turnaround on contracts, against what Moritz cites as an industry standard of at least three weeks. Everything around the legal work, from intake and quoting to staffing and follow-up, lives in Slack, with a thread per matter and a channel per client.</p><p>Now everyone from the CEO to paralegals asks Claude first. Questions that took up to 30 minutes of searching in Slack get answered in under two. The end-of-shift update, now drafted from the day’s threads, went from about an hour of assembly to a five-minute edit.</p><p>That time goes back to legal work. Claude Tag handles the administrative work around a case, like follow-up questions, reminders, and status updates. It can’t access client documents or privileged conversations with Moritz’s lawyers.</p><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/39f487100b408fabef0773334afb8c15e050525f.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“A firm working across 44 countries generates hundreds of one-off questions a month that no one will ever build a feature for. Claude Tag answers them from our own history in Slack. Every answer is a thread with links, so institutional memory compounds.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Stefan Mandaric, co-founder and CTO at Moritz</p></figcaption></figure><h3>Campfire: Customer experience on demand</h3><p>One Slack channel in particular “exploded in popularity”: their CX (or customer experience) channel. Sales uses this channel “to validate certain functionality during prospect conversations,” rather than having to “ping 10 different people.”</p><p>This type of channel is particularly effective because sales can answer in the moment, while the customer is paying attention, and can operate more independently and confidently in early customer conversations.</p><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/921fd10de481a1094bdd4b483f52933e68791fb2.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“Claude Tag basically acts as our central knowledge base.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Nancy Jin, AI engineering manager at Campfire</p></figcaption></figure><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapter"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterHead"><h2 id="chapter-4" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterTitle"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterNumber">04<!-- --> </span>Self-serve data</h2><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterValue ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterCopy"><div><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterParagraph text-body-3">@Claude remember for this channel: answer from our governed models and the definitions in [data skills repo]. If the data isn’t covered there, say it’s unvalidated instead of guessing. Lead with the answer, then give the number, what’s driving it, and any caveat. Check recent incidents, releases, and Slack discussions before explaining a change. If a metric’s definition is unclear, ask which one we mean. For anything important, share your plan or SQL before you run it. Separate what you verified from what you assumed, and list any open data quality warnings at the end of your answer. If someone finds a mistake, draft a fix for a data team member to review. If a question comes up twice, suggest scheduling it.</p></div><button type="button" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__copyButton" aria-label="Copy"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 3C13.3284 3 14 3.67157 14 4.5V6H15.5C16.3284 6 17 6.67157 17 7.5V15.5C17 16.3284 16.3284 17 15.5 17H7.5C6.67157 17 6 16.3284 6 15.5V14H4.5C3.67157 14 3 13.3284 3 12.5V4.5C3 3.67157 3.67157 3 4.5 3H12.5ZM14 12.5C14 13.3284 13.3284 14 12.5 14H7V15.5C7 15.7761 7.22386 16 7.5 16H15.5C15.7761 16 16 15.7761 16 15.5V7.5C16 7.22386 15.7761 7 15.5 7H14V12.5ZM4.5 4C4.22386 4 4 4.22386 4 4.5V12.5C4 12.7761 4.22386 13 4.5 13H12.5C12.7761 13 13 12.7761 13 12.5V4.5C13 4.22386 12.7761 4 12.5 4H4.5Z" /></svg></button></div></div></div></div><p>At a fast-growing startup every function wants numbers, and the data team has to decide whose request comes first. With Claude Tag connected to your data, anyone can ask in plain English without waiting in the data team’s queue.</p><p>This is a use case we have adopted as well. <a href="https://claude.com/resources/articles/self-service-data-analytics-in-slack-how-anthropic-deploys-claude-tag-for-ad-hoc-questions">In one of our data channels over a month, Claude Tag answered more than 75% of questions people posted, typically within a minute or two</a>. It works from governed data and the same definitions analysts use, which live in a versioned repo that Claude re-reads in every conversation.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:2024px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/4cf8ac80c074a4f3b28e78bd605ec9a881a611a8.png" width="2024" height="1016" alt="Diagram showing Claude Tag combining what moved in the warehouse with why from a knowledge index into one answer about a dip in sign-ups." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>From Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions.</figcaption></figure><h3>Descript: Answering ad-hoc data requests</h3><p>Descript is an AI-powered video editing platform. Claude Tag is now the first line of support for data requests and initial analyses. Product, growth, RevOps, and finance ask questions in Slack and get answers grounded in Descript’s dbt models.</p><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/93f058c356e58c0f49205fd19e8f3585533542bf.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“I used to write complicated SQL and refresh the numbers by hand every week or month. Now I’ve replaced several data-team dashboards with my own Claude artifacts, and I no longer refresh them by hand.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Daisy Zhang, head of growth marketing at Descript</p></figcaption></figure><p>Daisy’s recurring reporting prep went from days to hours.</p><p>The growth team, for example, asks why lifecycle subscriptions dropped, whether paid search is losing last-touch credit to other channels, or how long a self-serve account takes to become an enterprise opportunity. The data team tracks the artifacts Claude generates to see which data assets matter most across teams, and spends its own time on strategic questions and on building the context that makes self-serve work.</p><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/04cc4542c1f0cb9d273d22b2597f8e856abe542a.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“The promise of business intelligence has always been self-serve for business users. I’d never seen it actually realized until we had Claude Tag set up with immense context for our data.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Jen Huhn, monetization PM at Descript</p></figcaption></figure><aside class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tip"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipInner"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipEyebrow"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipText"><h3 class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipTitle text-headline-6-serif">Invest in context first.</h3><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipParagraph text-body-3">Have your data team document the core models and metric definitions, because self-serve is only as good as the context Claude has. See <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/users/use-cases/answer-data-questions">Answer data questions</a>.</p></div></div></aside><h3>Orderful: From question to dashboard</h3><p>At Orderful, self-serve analytics spans conversational analytics and full data builds: anyone can go from a question in Slack to a dashboard merged to production. The key is a semantic layer that encodes agreed definitions and metrics, so every answer and every build uses the same definitions.</p><figure class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quote"><img class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quotePhoto" src="https://assets.claude.com/ae41953c096037ea0d3a369b9af1e1f52378367a.jpg?w=168&amp;q=75&amp;fm=webp&amp;fit=max" alt="" width="56" height="56" loading="lazy" decoding="async" referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"/><blockquote class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteText"><p class="text-body-1-serif">“We trust the output because a semantic layer constrains the SQL, CI gates the builds, and there’s a process for agreeing on definitions. Without those, you get confident-looking wrong answers. Once those guardrails were in place, connecting Claude Tag took under 30 minutes. Now teammates build together in shared Slack threads instead of solo sessions.”</p></blockquote><figcaption class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__quoteAttribution"><p class="text-body-3">Piers MacDonald, CTO at Orderful</p></figcaption></figure><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapter"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterHead"><h2 id="chapter-5" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterTitle"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterNumber">05<!-- --> </span>Reporting and handoffs</h2><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterSubtitle text-body-1">Example setups:</p></div><div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterRow"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterKey text-caption"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8.99962 2C12.3133 2 14.9996 4.68629 14.9996 8C14.9996 11.3137 12.3133 14 8.99962 14H2.49962C2.30105 13.9998 2.12113 13.8821 2.04161 13.7002C1.96224 13.5181 1.99835 13.3058 2.1334 13.1602L3.93516 11.2178C3.34317 10.2878 2.99962 9.18343 2.99962 8C2.99962 4.68643 5.68609 2.00022 8.99962 2ZM8.99962 3C6.23838 3.00022 3.99961 5.23871 3.99961 8C3.99961 9.11212 4.36265 10.1386 4.97618 10.9688C5.11884 11.1621 5.1035 11.4293 4.94004 11.6055L3.64512 13H8.99962C11.761 13 13.9996 10.7614 13.9996 8C13.9996 5.23858 11.761 3 8.99962 3Z" />

Lead with what changed and what needs a decision. Separate what you verified from what you assumed, and flag anything missing instead of filling the gap. Post the draft in its own thread for [owner] to edit. Nothing goes out until a person approves it. If a report keeps getting the same edits, suggest updating these instructions.</p></div><button type="button" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__copyButton" aria-label="Copy"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 3C13.3284 3 14 3.67157 14 4.5V6H15.5C16.3284 6 17 6.67157 17 7.5V15.5C17 16.3284 16.3284 17 15.5 17H7.5C6.67157 17 6 16.3284 6 15.5V14H4.5C3.67157 14 3 13.3284 3 12.5V4.5C3 3.67157 3.67157 3 4.5 3H12.5ZM14 12.5C14 13.3284 13.3284 14 12.5 14H7V15.5C7 15.7761 7.22386 16 7.5 16H15.5C15.7761 16 16 15.7761 16 15.5V7.5C16 7.22386 15.7761 7 15.5 7H14V12.5ZM4.5 4C4.22386 4 4 4.22386 4 4.5V12.5C4 12.7761 4.22386 13 4.5 13H12.5C12.7761 13 13 12.7761 13 12.5V4.5C13 4.22386 12.7761 4 12.5 4H4.5Z" /></svg></button></div></div></div></div><p>Many of the examples we’ve covered are reactive: something happens, Claude responds. Routine reporting is work Claude owns on a schedule, the way a teammate owns a recurring deliverable.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:1809px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/8d3d8fd8252fc93f3bd80bb28ae0a728142a7ef2.png" width="1809" height="1491" alt="Slack exchange in which a teammate asks Claude for a Monday pipeline update, and Claude posts a weekly digest with a chart." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>Example of using Routines in Claude Tag.</figcaption></figure><p>You describe the outcome once; Claude runs it every time and posts the result where the team already works.</p><h3>Valence: Deal reviews and handoffs</h3><p>Valence is setting Claude up to brief the team before every quarterly business review, with customer health, open deals, blockers, and next steps. They are also working to make the handoff from sales to customer success when a deal closes more seamless. Claude saves the team time by helping to aggregate details across their engagement and often finds key items they may have missed.</p><p>“When a deal closes, Tag builds the handoff from the deal history, calls and contract: who’s who, what was promised, what’s customized, and what’s still open. Customer success then reviews it before their kickoff,” said Sameer.</p><aside class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tip"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipInner"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipEyebrow"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" 8.08203L7.85352 8.14648L10 10.293L12.1465 8.14648L12.2246 8.08203C12.4187 7.95387 12.6827 7.97562 12.8535 8.14648C13.0244 8.31735 13.0461 8.58131 12.918 8.77539L12.8535 8.85352L10.5 class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipText"><h3 class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipTitle text-headline-6-serif">If you’ve asked it twice, schedule it.</h3><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__tipParagraph text-body-3">“@Claude every Monday at 9am Eastern, post a brief on each account with a QBR this month: health, open deals, blockers, and next steps.” See <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/users/proactivity">Set up routines</a>.</p></div></div></aside><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapter"><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterHead"><h2 id="chapter-6" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterTitle"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterNumber">06<!-- --> </span>Getting started checklist</h2><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__chapterSubtitle text-body-1">The checklist below pulls together these startup teams’ best practices so you can apply them to your own workflows.</p></div></div><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklist"><div><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistGroup text-body-2-serif">Before launch</p><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Check the prerequisites.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Claude Tag is in public beta on Claude Team and Enterprise plans, and isn’t available on Free, Pro, or Max. You’ll need a Claude organization Owner and a Slack workspace admin to connect the two. An admin must also turn on Routines, and Team plans need usage credits before Claude responds.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Set up Claude’s access with a bundle.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">In channels, Claude works under its own <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/agent-identity">agent identity</a>, with service accounts rather than anyone’s personal login. Group the connectors, repos, and instructions it needs in a <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/add-connections">bundle</a>, and attach them org-wide, per workspace, or per channel. That sets what Claude can reach in each place, and everyone in a channel gets the same access. Start narrow: only what the first channel’s job needs.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Experiment in a private channel.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Nearly half the startups we spoke with started their Claude Tag journey by having a small cross-functional team experiment in a private channel. “Start private with a mix of roles, then move to a group channel,” said Sameer.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Determine the boundaries.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">By default, anyone in your Slack workspace can use Claude, even without a Claude account. You can <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/restrict-access">restrict access</a> to your org and limit search to channels Claude is in. On Enterprise, you can also restrict access to specific roles or chosen channels.</p><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Set clear expectations for what Claude can do and can never do. Several teams we spoke with let Claude open draft PRs, but people review and merge. For Orderful, <a href="https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-code-guide-for-startups">Claude Code</a>, not Tag, handles “infrastructure changes, audits, sensitive data.” For a “hard call,” such as “a PR that touches more than one service,” Claude gets a second opinion. Moritz doesn’t give Claude Tag access to client documents or privileged conversations with its lawyers.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Start your security review early.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">The usual questions are data retention and what Claude can reach, and the <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/security-and-data">security</a> and <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/data-lifecycle">data lifecycle</a> pages answer both. Claude Tag isn’t available to orgs with zero data retention turned on, a customer-managed encryption (CMEK) policy, or the HIPAA configuration, and it isn’t covered by our Business Associate Agreement, so check that before you plan a rollout.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Set a budget and alerts.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Claude Tag bills by usage, so an early conversation avoids surprises as adoption grows. You can <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/set-spend-limit">set spend limits</a> overall and per channel, choose the model per channel, and <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/attribute-costs">attribute costs</a> by user using the Enterprise Analytics API. Orderful runs an org-wide cap with alerts at 75% and 90%. “We have extreme ownership on the channel costs. The owner justifies that ‘yes, this spend is reasonable for the output / outcomes,’” said Alex Dejeu, engineering manager at Kikoff. Use your first channel’s actual costs to size the next one.</p></span></span></label></div></div><figure><div class="Video-module-scss-module__miVj5a__video Video-module-scss-module__miVj5a__youtubeEmbed Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__video" data-youtube-id="JhipXUs1Y98"><iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/JhipXUs1Y98?enablejsapi=1&amp;rel=0&amp;playsinline=1&amp;modestbranding=1" title="Agent identity: A new access model for Claude Tag" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-presentation allow-popups" allowFullScreen="" class="Video-module-scss-module__miVj5a__player"></iframe></div></figure><div class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklist"><div><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistGroup text-body-2-serif">Deployment</p><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Pick one clear task in a channel your team already uses, like on-call alerts or bug triage.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">“We experiment on certain teams, see what works, then once confident we’ve worked out the kinks, we push the idea out to other teams to add to their own similar channels as well. We want to avoid trust breaking experiences with folks with lower tolerance to AI mistakes,” said Alex Dejeu, engineering manager at Kikoff.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Prime your experts and culture bearers.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Have the people your team already trusts use Claude first, and in the open.</p><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">“Going back and forth with Claude in the open has been productive and fun. Several people in sales and customer success have watched experts [interact with Claude Tag], then started asking Claude themselves, and got value fast,” said Sameer Bansal, principal AI engineer at Valence.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Tune the noise.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Multiple startups told us they needed to adjust Claude’s chattiness. Too chatty is one risk.</p><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">“Conversation in ad hoc requests can sometimes get noisy. We’ve been trying to tune down the responsiveness here and also be more principled on what we use Claude on ad hoc requests for,” said Mike Chen, head of engineering at NavigateAI.</p><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Too little chattiness is also a risk, however. In busy channels, “You either have to @ every time or it won’t do much,” said Will Hu, cofounder at Flagler Health. And “if no one is watching a channel closely or interacts with it, it will sit idle.”</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 14.8202C8.29361 14.9279 8.16242 14.9925 8.02221 14.9989C7.88203 15.0051 7.74545 14.9526 7.64622 14.8534L4.14617 11.3533L4.08172 11.2752C3.95384 11.0811 3.97542 10.817 4.14617 10.6463C4.31693 10.4755 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Have teammates connect their own accounts.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">The admin bundles from setup are what Claude can reach for everyone in a channel. <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/personal-connectors">Personal connectors</a> work differently: Claude acts with the permissions of the person asking, so it can pull from their docs, inbox, or CRM once they approve it (an Owner adds the connector for the org first, and on Enterprise an admin manages personal connectors). The answer still posts in the channel, so choose “Allow with review” for anything sensitive.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15.1883 5.10908C15.3699 4.96398 15.6346 4.96153 15.8202 5.11592C16.0056 5.27067 16.0504 5.53125 15.9403 5.73605L15.8836 5.82003L8.38354 4.58105 10.4539 4.77509 10.5818L4.85321 10.6463L7.96556 13.7586L15.1161 5.1794L15.1883 5.10908Z" /></svg></span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistText"><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Write channel instructions like you’re onboarding a new hire:</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">what to check first, when to open a PR, when to ask, and that “no action needed” is a valid answer.</p></span></span></label><label class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistItem"><input type="checkbox" class="sr-only"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistBox"><svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistTitle text-body-3">Give Claude feedback in the channel, not in DMs.</span><span class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistDescription text-body-3"><p class="ArticleBlocks-module-scss-module__bq-ZvW__checklistParagraph">Correct it in the thread. It <a href="https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/users/memory">remembers per channel</a>, and teammates learn how to work with it by watching. For a lasting fix, ask Claude to update its memory for this channel.</p></span></span></label></div></div><figure style="--media-natural-width:2100px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/7e4a82b6f73aabecf6a5a5fe148c38a53659ba7a.png" width="2100" height="756" alt="Two Slack messages from Valence employees thanking a colleague for working through a question with Claude in the open." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>Two Valence employees thank a colleague after watching them work through a question with Claude in the open. Used with permission from Valence.</figcaption></figure><p>Not sure where to go next? Tag Claude and ask what it has learned about your org and which use cases it would expand to.</p><p>Moritz’s co-founder and CTO, Stefan Mandaric, asked Claude to recommend use cases for each team. Fifteen minutes later, it had read the firm’s Slack channels, Linear issues, Notion SOPs, Drive, and Metabase dashboards, and published 25. “18 of 25 worked with no further setup. That became our rollout plan.”</p><hr/><h2 id="last-word-what-we-learned-from-the-wow-moments">Last word: what we learned from the wow moments</h2><p>The wow moments weren’t always about speed. Often, Claude found something no one had asked it to look for. Sometimes the surprise was restraint. And sometimes the surprise was the unexpected exchanges. “Eventually you get used to Claude jumping in on jokes, and you soon appreciate that it’s an easy audience and the first one to laugh,” said Piers MacDonald, CTO at Orderful.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:2048px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/8884ca89d9b6e0bf91eb7b426d8546c971d8079d.png" width="2048" height="821" alt="Slack thread with an image reply and reactions." loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>Recreated Orderful conversation in Slack. Used with permission from Orderful.</figcaption></figure><p>We hope you found this guide useful. Special thanks to Campfire, Descript, Flagler Health, Kikoff, Moritz, NavigateAI, Orderful and Valence for sharing their experiences and insights.</p><hr/><h2 id="additional-resources">Additional
